messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: P1 INF-7523 - elevated latency + 5xx across inference gateway; majority of error budget traced to structured-output/tool-call paths. Triggered at 2026-03-14T22:16:07Z
olivia (oncall): I'm seeing continuous spikes on rpc latency for /v1/chat with tools enabled. Errors are downstream timeouts from tool execution layer. Dashboard -> https://console.redwood.internal/d/latency/structured-output
mike (sre): Confirmed. 95th token latency up x6, queue lengths growing on gpu-pool-3. Looks like a surge of long tool-call chains + heavy kv-cache churn.
aubrey (pm): Any customer-facing impact? Support seeing uptick in complaints?
nora (support): A handful of enterprise customers reported degraded responses, some timed out. No mass outage yet but top customers on Hosted tier see slower interactive responses.
olivia (oncall): Initial mitigation: apply conservative rate limit to tool/call endpoints while we triage. I'll page infra to throttle at ingress to preserve non-tool chat traffic.
sam (sre): Good. Suggest also toggling structured-output webhook/truncation to prevent huge payloads. If needed we can disable tool.function_calling for the Hosted tier only (leave Dedicated).
mike (sre): Quick plan: 1) soft-rate-limit tool calls to 5 rps per customer 2) enforce token cap for structured outputs 3) temporarily disable function calling on Hosted API key pool. Implement in that order so we don't disrupt Dedicated customers. Thoughts?
aubrey (pm): Prioritize customer impact minimal. Start with rate-limiting first. If that fails, toggle function calls for non-enterprise keys. Communicate to support.
olivia (oncall): Executing rate-limit rule now (ingress controller). Command:```sh
# add per-customer rate-limit for /v1/chat/tool_call
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/ratelimits"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"route": "/v1/chat/tool_call", "limit": 5, "window_seconds": 1, "scope": "customer"}'
```
mike (sre): Rule applied. Observability: queues stopped growing, p95 came down slightly. But we're still at elevated CPU on gpu-pool-3.
nora (support): I'm posting an update to affected customers: "We've applied temporary rate limits to tool calls to improve stability; engineers are investigating."
olivia (oncall): Next: apply token cap for structured outputs to 2048 tokens on Hosted. Command (internal flag):```sh
redwoodctl feature-flag set structured_output_max_tokens=2048 --env=prod
```
sam (sre): Flag set confirmed by deploy-bot. (deploy-bot reaction :white_check_mark:)
mike (sre): OK still seeing a subset of requests causing backend timeouts — looks like some requests are invoking chains of functions that call external HTTPs and wait. We should flip function calling off for non-paid/hosted keys while keeping enterprise exemptions.
aubrey (pm): typo in handle, ignore
aubrey (pm): Let's be explicit about exemptions: enterprise tags (enterprise: true) and Dedicated clusters should be excluded.
olivia (oncall): Preparing toggle. Internal ops endpoint supports scoped toggles. Example payload: ```json
{"flag": "enable_tool_calls", "value": false, "scope": {"tier": "hosted", "exclude_tags": ["enterprise"]}}
```
mike (sre): Nice. Execute and monitor. Also push temporary dashboard note and status page entry.
olivia (oncall): Executing toggle now via ops API:```sh
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/flags/toggle"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"flag":"enable_tool_calls","value":false,"scope":{"tier":"hosted","exclude_tags":["enterprise"]}}'
```
deploy-bot: Feature flag change accepted: enable_tool_calls=false (scope: hosted, exclude enterprise). Propagating to edge proxies and runtime.
sam (sre): Flag rolled, proxies picked up change, 5xxs from tool paths dropped ~85% within 2m. p95 overall latency back to normal range.
nora (support): Sending customer follow-up: "We've temporarily restricted tool/function calling for hosted keys to stabilize latency. Enterprise and Dedicated customers unaffected. We'll update when we re-enable."
aubrey (pm): Good. Need a postmortem: how did a small subset of callers cause such broad kv cache churn? Add evals to detect long function chains.
mike (sre): Agreed. Also add a permanent guard: deny more than 3 nested function calls per request in the router. I'll file infra ticket.
olivia (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 20m — sam will own monitoring, escalation, and rollback plan. Sam, are you good to take P1?
sam (sre): I'm on it. I'll watch for errors and coordinate with infra. If we see any regression, plan is: 1) rollback rate-limit to previous if latency improves but errors persist 2) re-enable function calls selectively for affected enterprise customers via tag 3) postmortem w/owner.
olivia (oncall): Thanks. Final note: scheduled follow-up with PM/Support in 2 hours to craft customer comms and timeline for re-enablement.
incident-bot: Incident INF-7523 acknowledged by sam.
nora (support): Updated ticketing: added list of affected customers + timestamps.
aubrey (pm): Thank you all — good triage. Please collect logs and example requests for postmortem.
sam (sre): copying logs to internal bucket: s3://ops-logs/INF-7523/ and creating postmortem draft. I'll ping everyone once draft is up.
olivia (oncall): Leaving thread. :wave:
